improv_extras.concept: fold the point cloud through an iterated-function-system (affine contractions + rotation) so a self-similar fractal structure emerges

v1.feedback: The Barnsley fern is cleanly implemented with an excellent restrained moss/olive/cream palette and gentle breeze animation, but the chain lineage from calyx (6mk) is invisible — this reads as a fresh fern, not a calyx that's been fractalized by 'IFS fractal fold'. A stronger chain morph might start from the calyx's cup-shaped geometry and gradually unfurl fractal fronds from its rim. The leaf-shaped point sprites with midrib veins are a nice touch, but the form is essentially flat (z ±0.35); giving the fronds real depth curvature or a slight spiral around the stem would add dimensionality and distinguish it from the textbook 2D Barnsley example.

v2.feedback: The calyx-to-fern-frond chain reads well — the cupped base with Riley interference bands preserves 6mk lineage while the IFS fronds unfurling from petal rims genuinely embody 'fractal fold'. Palette (bone/umber cup, olive-to-moss fronds) is properly restrained. Two improvements: the frond tips thin out to near-invisibility due to the opacity falloff combined with shrinking point size — consider keeping point size constant at ~2.2px across the frond and letting density alone communicate the fractal taper. Second, the concave curvature term (-rawLat² × 0.012) is too subtle to read as leaf curl at this scale; doubling it would give the fronds the gutter-channel depth that sells 'botanical surface' rather than 'flat fern decal'.
